title: Token-throttle queue deadlock during cross-region failover — mitigation & follow-up
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a planned failover of primary region us-east-1 to us-west-2 (triggered by maintenance), the token-based throttle queue subsystem entered a deadlocked state for ~14 minutes. This caused large numbers of requests to receive 429s and exacerbated downstream backlog on routing proxies. Several high-volume customers experienced partial outage symptoms (increased errors and degraded throughput).

Scope: The incident affected the API gateway rate limiter (token-throttle path) only during cross-region active-active handoff. Non-gateway services and internal control plane remained nominal.
impact_summary: Approximately 11% increase in 429s across gateway traffic for the 14 minute window, 4 large customers observed client-visible errors, and cost increased slightly due to retry traffic. No data loss. Customer support tickets created: 5 (2 escalated).
timeline:
2025-02-18 02:03 UTC — Planned maintenance initiated for us-east-1
2025-02-18 02:07 UTC — Health checks began failing on a subset of gateway enforcers in us-east-1 as traffic drained
2025-02-18 02:09 UTC — Automated failover began; control plane instructed us-west-2 enforcers to pick up token buckets
2025-02-18 02:09:30 UTC — Token-throttle queue worker observed backlog growth; worker threads blocked trying to acquire token-store locks
2025-02-18 02:12 UTC — Error rates spike, automated alert (rate-limiter-429-threshold) fires
2025-02-18 02:13 UTC — On-call rotates to SRE; initial mitigation: scale up enforcer replicas in us-west-2 (manual)
2025-02-18 02:18 UTC — Manual restart of the token-throttle service on 3 pods clears the deadlock condition
2025-02-18 02:23 UTC — 429 rates return to baseline; traffic normalizes
2025-02-18 03:00 UTC — Incident declared mitigated and postmortem assigned
root_cause: Race in token-store handoff during active-active failover: concurrent handoff and token-bucket compaction led to lock inversion between reorder-queue thread and the persistent token snapshot writer. Under the sudden surge of transferred tokens during failover, the reorder queue blocked waiting for a snapshot write while the snapshot writer awaited the queue drain, producing a deadlock. The locking discipline change introduced in gateway-2.13.1 (concurrent compaction optimization) reduced lock grip time in steady-state but introduced an inversion during handoff edge cases.
short_term_mitigation: Revert the compaction ordering change in gateway-2.13.1 for token-store handoff (hotfix gateway-2.13.2)
Add a fail-open path for enforcers during regional handoff: briefly accept requests with a soft-throttle and emit telemetry instead of blocking
Increase readiness probe timeout to avoid premature failover triggers while token handoff completes
Operational playbook update: on token-throttle deadlock alerts, restart token-throttle pods in affected region before scaling
Customer comms: notify impacted customers with timeline and remediation steps
long_term_action_items: Redesign token-store lock hierarchy to eliminate inversion (ENG-45340) — owner: Platform Storage
Implement handoff coordination protocol with idempotent snapshot transfers and explicit handoff tokens
Add comprehensive chaos tests for cross-region failover involving token-throttle and KV compaction
Introduce non-blocking snapshot writer backed by lock-free buffer to tolerate transient queue drains
Surge testing exercise: repeat cross-region failover with production traffic shapes in staging
Add observability: per-bucket queue depth histograms, handoff latency SLI, and deadlock detection metric
rollout_plan: Hotfix gateway-2.13.2 containing revert to be rolled to a canary cohort of 10% traffic in both regions for 2 hours (smoke checks: 429 rate, queue depth, CPU). If stable, progressive rollout to 50% then 100% over 24 hours. Long-term changes to land behind feature flags and gated with chaos and canary runs in staging before global rollout.
verification_metrics: 429 rate (gateway overall) — target: <= baseline + 0.5% after rollout
Token-throttle queue depth median and p95 — target: no unexplained spikes during simulated handoff
Number of deadlock-detection alerts — target: 0 in 30d post-change
